root_idea.summary: The root centers on something enclosing, surrounding, or bounded around another thing.
root_idea.development: From this orientation arise the eye's dark central part set within the surrounding white, fixed or intense looking, encircling, and the garden as a bounded or watered tract. The garden term is also explained through resemblance to the eye in form and in the presence of water.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested broken plural is normalized to the classical singular citation form حديقة.

senses.definition: A garden or watered, cultivated tract of land; in the Quran, gardens.
senses.usage_conditions: The attested Quranic form is the broken plural حَدَائِقُ, occurring in the supplied locations as حَدَآئِقَ. The Quran-focused explanation describes the حديقة as a piece of land containing water and relates its naming to the eye in form and in the presence of water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To look at something; of a group, to fix their eyes on someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form I. The expression may describe people casting the blacks of their eyes toward someone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hit or hurt the black of the eye.
Of a dying person, to open the eyes and move or twinkle the eyelids.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A usage specifically reported of one who is dying.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To look intently, rolling or displaying the black of the eye.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II; used with the object of the gaze, commonly with إِلَى.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To surround, encompass, encircle, or go round something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Often constructed with بِـ. It may be said of people, a town, a wall, a house, death, or other things; the eye-specific expression includes making the blacks of the eyes surround someone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a meadow, to become a garden by producing herbage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV intransitive usage describing the transformation of a meadow into a حديقة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A collective term for the fruit of the eggplant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported botanical or collective-noun usage; a variant spelling with ذ is noted but not established.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The black or central round part of the eye; by extension, sometimes the eye as a whole.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Descriptions distinguish the larger black portion from the pupil or central ناظر, while other accounts use the term for the eye more broadly. Its plurals include أَحْدَاق, حَدَقَات, and حِدَاق. Expressions also describe people looking at a speaker, and refer to accurate throwers or shooters in an associated idiom.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A moisture-rich tract abounding in herbage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative usage comparing such a tract with the moist eye of a camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A walled, fenced, or otherwise bounded garden or planted plot; by extension, a garden or tree-filled meadow, including a palm grove, orchard, vineyard, or crop plot.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may also denote a distinct collection of palm trees. It is used figuratively of garden-like beauty or language.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hollow or depressed place in a valley that retains water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A topographical extension of the garden term; water need not still be present in the depression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A large or prominent eye, especially one whose globe or black projects noticeably.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used adjectivally of an eye and compared with جَاحِظَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A reported term for an otherwise unidentified body part; one account identifies it as the epiglottis.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The identification is uncertain and attributed to particular speakers or authorities.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A difficult or distressing affair or event that causes people to look intently.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantivized active-participle usage describing an alarming circumstance.

cautions: The Quranic public headword is normalized to the singular حَدِيقَة, while the attested Quranic form is its broken plural حَدَائِق. Classical descriptions extend حديقة beyond a walled garden to broader garden, meadow, crop-plot, and topographical uses; those extensions are kept separate from the Quran-attested watered-garden sense.
